facts.name: Sweet Joe-Pye Weed
facts.notes: A big, stately back-row plant with vanilla-scented flower domes that are a butterfly magnet in late summer.

sources.title: Designs By Nature: Sweet Joe-Pye Weed
Penn State Extension: Cutting Down Perennials in the Fall
sources.note: Cut peonies, daylilies, brunnera and speedwell in fall; cut bee balm and garden phlox with powdery mildew and destroy the leaves; rake up hosta leaves (slug eggs); cut yarrow and Shasta daisy flower stalks but keep the base leaves. Leave grasses, Siberian iris, baptisia, sedum, Joe-Pye weed, coneflower, black-eyed Susan and most natives standing; leave marginally hardy anise hyssop tops over winter; tidy hardy geraniums, heucheras, hellebores and moss phlox in spring.

companions.why: Pair with fall aster, bugbane, eupatorium, goldenrod, sedum or toad lily; near bleeding heart; with variegated hosta and grasses.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Japanese Anemone article

companions.why: New Moon Nurseries: try pairing with swamp milkweed, turtlehead, Joe-Pye weed (Eupatorium purpureum) or great blue lobelia.
